➥ नेशनल स्कॉलरशिप पोर्टल (NSP) पर सेंट्रल सेक्टर स्कॉलरशिप (CSS) योजना के अंतर्गत शैक्षणिक सत्र 2026-27 के लिए आवेदन प्रक्रिया शुरू कर दी गई है। फिलहाल पोर्टल पर 2024-28 एवं 2025-29 सत्र के उन विद्यार्थियों के लिए नवीनीकरण (Renewal) आवेदन की सुविधा उपलब्ध कराई गई है, जो पहले से इस छात्रवृत्ति का लाभ प्राप्त कर रहे हैं।

➥ विद्यार्थी NSP पोर्टल पर लॉगिन कर अपने नवीनीकरण आवेदन की प्रक्रिया पूरी कर सकते हैं। ध्यान दें कि नवीनीकरण (Renewal) केवल उन्हीं विद्यार्थियों का होगा, जिनकी छात्रवृत्ति राशि (Scholarship Payment) पूर्व में स्वीकृत होकर उनके खाते में प्राप्त हो चुकी है। जिन विद्यार्थियों को अब तक छात्रवृत्ति भुगतान प्राप्त नहीं हुआ है, वे फिलहाल नवीनीकरण आवेदन के पात्र नहीं होंगे।

❓ What Should Be the Next Step After Prelims for Mains 2026 ❓

https://youtu.be/cae_tJvZflI?si=alYCdzgSC9fNtXx1

📣 Many students are asking: “Sir, what should be my next step after Prelims?” This doubt is natural, especially for first-time and second-time aspirants.

✍️ If you are scoring around 60–70 marks, you should immediately start serious preparation for Mains. And even if you are not qualifying this year, this period between Prelims and Mains is still extremely valuable for building next year’s preparation.

The biggest mistake students make after Prelims is lack of direction. So your first task should be to systematically segregate the Mains syllabus.

⭐️ Step 1: Divide the Mains Syllabus into Two Parts

A. Subjects/Topics Common to Prelims and Mains

These include most portions of: GS Paper I GS Paper II GS Paper III

📌 Conceptually and factually, you have already studied a major part of these during Prelims' preparation.

B. Mains-Specific Subjects/Topics

These are areas that require a different orientation: Society, Ethics, Essay, Optional Subject, Internal Security, Disaster Management, World History, Post-Independence History

These topics demand analytical, applied, and answer-writing-oriented preparation.

⭐️ Step 2: Further Divide Mains-Specific Areas

1.Major Mains-Specific Subjects : These are high-scoring and high-weightage areas: Ethics, Society, Essay, Optional Subject

2.Minor Mains-Specific Subjects : These are comparatively smaller portions: World History, Post-Independence History, Internal Security, Disaster Management

⭐️ Step 3: Follow the Correct Sequence

First Focus On: Ethic, Optional,  Society, Essay, 

Then Move to,  Internal Security, Disaster Management, World History, Post-Independence History

Finally, Revise, GS topics common to Prelims and Mains

💬 Why So ❓
For the last five months, you have already been studying GS 1, 2, 3 - oriented content. Your conceptual base and factual matrix are already prepared. Now you only need: application, answer writing, problem-solving orientation.

✔️ A Very Important Reality About GS Scores

💙 If you analyse marks of many toppers in: GS1, GS2, GS3,

you will notice that average scores are often moderate.

Even among top ranks, several students score in double digits in some GS papers, and the majority  remain below 50% marks. This trend is not from one year only — it has continued over multiple years.
So understand carefully: GS1, GS2, and GS3 have limited scope for extraordinary score jumps.

Therefore, do not become hyper-competitive in these papers. Do not waste disproportionate time chasing perfection there.

Trust your Prelims preparation foundation for performance in these papers.

Where Can You Actually Create Rank Difference? Real scoring potential lies in ethics, Essay, Optional Subject. These papers create differentiation.

That is where serious aspirants separate themselves from the crowd.

🏆 The Problem with Blindly Following Topper Copies

Today, there is a trend: topper copies, model answers, mentor templates, “ideal answer formats”.

But ask yourself honestly, if a topper himself scored average marks in a paper, then blindly imitating that copy will not suddenly produce extraordinary marks for you.

Many so-called model answers in the market look almost identical:

same structure, same examples, same language, same buzzwords. This creates uniformity, not differentiation.

🚨Whom Should You Follow?
Follow toppers selectively.

Study answer copies of students who actually scored 120+ 125+ exceptionally well in specific papers. For example: students scoring 118–125 in GS3, 124–126 in GS2, and high marks in Ethics or Essay.
Those copies deserve serious analysis.

🔥 Final  Message Do not remain stuck in random guidance, excessive strategy videos, blind imitation, endless topper discussions.

That is the real next step after Prelims.
